claim: research-tree/tools/lane.mjs re-reads capacity.txt (clamped to 1..4, 1 when unreadable) at every 700 ms poll but tries only slots 0 to n-1, so after the count is lowered a holder of a higher slot is not counted and a waiter can take slot-0: more commands run than the new count until that holder ends.

lane.mjs breaks a held slot when its owner's pid is dead, its hold is older than 20 minutes (counted from owner.json's time, no heartbeat), or owner.json cannot be read and the folder is older than 15 s; owner.json is written in place, not by rename, and the break has no fence, so two waiters that judge one slot stale can each remove it and the second deletes the first's fresh slot.

A lane command's timeout may be set up to 1,500 s (25 minutes) while a live holder loses its slot after 20 minutes; the longest command in the lane log (r3-q5b-parts, 25.0 minutes) was a timeout kill, exit 124 at 1,500,104 ms on 2026-11-17, and the same label's run before it ended at 1,193,636 ms (19.9 minutes).

The lane log carries the wait on every start line (waited_ms, with the pid) and the run time on every end line (ms), but a queued command leaves no line until it starts or gives up (one 'busy' line in 1,577 lines), and no line carries the slot count.

research-tree/tools/recorder.ps1 writes one line every 2 s with the time of day only (free memory, whole-PC processor share, process, node and powershell counts), ends itself after 12 hours, and is started by hand (no script, task or hook starts it); its log covers three periods of 2026-11-17 local time, 03:11 to 07:34, 12:07 to 15:45:34 and 17:19:03 to 21:51:16, and had no line since when read on 2026-11-18.

claim: The recorder's governor stops only node.exe or powershell.exe processes whose command line holds 'tcb-build' (when free memory is under 2,500 MB, node over 60, powershell over 40, or the processor hot for 30 s); no lane command line has held that name since 2026-11-17T08:42Z, so it matches nothing today, it runs only while the hand-started recorder runs, and recorder.log holds no GOVERNOR line.

The tier hook acts on PreToolUse only, looks only at helper (Agent) and start_session calls and refuses by exit 2; an unreadable or unparsable routes file refuses every start, but routes that parse to null or a kind without models throw and exit 1, which lets the call through; it is wired only in this repository's project settings (the user settings have no hooks), so sessions in other folders never run it.
The tier hook's log line holds t, session, agent_id, what, kind, model and decision (label and why on a refusal): no token, memory or finish field.

Each helper has a meta file (subagents/agent-<id>.meta.json in its session's folder under the user's .claude/projects) holding its description, model and toolUseId, which gains a finished key when the helper ends; a missing key does not mean running: on 2026-11-18 the refuter found 11 of 404 meta files without it for helpers long ended (5 in one session of another project, transcripts silent since 01:06), and the fold's recount gave 12 of 405 with its own running helper among them.

Tokens per helper are on disk: research-tree/tcb/lib.mjs finds a session's helper transcripts by its id (agent-*.jsonl under the session's subagents folder) and spendOf sums tokens, peak and last context per transcript, so tokens per unit by kind and model can be counted without a run.

research-tree/tcb/admit.mjs decide is pure (no I/O, no clock) and caps live children at min(N_max, N_ceiling, 3), refusing an N_max above N_ceiling or 3 as 'ceiling' rather than clamping it; its memory term uses one flat peak for every session; its token-budget term applies only when B_tokens is set, and B_tokens is null, so it never refuses today.
evidence: research-tree/tcb/admit.mjs#line 16, line 137, lines 145-147, line 224, line 231, lines 237-243, line 258

claim: In research-tree/tcb/thresholds.json the numbers a width would use are guesses or unset: N_max 2, one session's peak 1,200 MB, the reserve 1,024 MB, 2 ticks to confirm a stop and a checker batch of 12 carry source 'guess'; B_tokens and r_tokens are null; the coordinator's hand-over window of 133,200 tokens is computed from estimates, not measured.
replace.mjs start runs admit's decide inside the run lock and defers a refusal with exit 6, and the admit ledger line records the live children and free memory (free_mb).

research-tree/tcb/watch.mjs works out slotFree once per tick from N_max alone (used < N_max) and passes it to every row, so one free slot can give several replace-start acts in one tick that admit may then defer; the watcher raises class 24 below the memory reserve, drains at the hand-over window, and makes a checker batch due at 12 candidates or when nothing else runs.

research-tree/tcb/check-queue.mjs orders checker items by field and card id, not by age, and its queue ledger line, written only when a batch is formed, carries batch, n, n_seeds and rng_seed: no waiting time.

research-tree/tcb/cost.mjs already computes the memory width floor((free - reserve) / rss) and prints it in its JSON and speed table, but no gate reads it; its unit-cost file leaves serial_fraction and memory null; it turns the first and last typed-in meter percents into tokens per point.

research-tree/tcb/lib.mjs edgeFacts is the tree's one place for clock, free memory (os.freemem), boot and process reads; its process query has no memory field; a session's processes are found by folder or session id in command lines, for reports only; ledger kinds are a closed list; the last attempt of a committed row holds one slot until its stop is confirmed.

claim: In the tree, guard-hook lets the coordinator run only node tcb/<name>.mjs, so lane.mjs is refused there; the tree's coordinator settings wire guard-hook (timeout 30 s, no onFailure) and not the tier hook; guard-hook loads lib by a guarded dynamic import so that a broken lib.mjs is a deny, never a crash with exit 1.

Three memory floors are in use on this PC and no other record names them together: 2,500 MB in the recorder's governor (which matches nothing today), 1,024 MB kept back by the tree's admit, and 4,000 MB in the model runner, which admits a part only while free memory less running headroom less the part's size stays above it and samples its own children's working set.

The tree's run-time writers share no work file: a child writes only its own staging folder, objects are stored by exclusive create and never repaired, two disagreeing verdicts make the item 'unclear', and the task table is written by compare-and-set on its revision.

The lane ran with one slot only from its first command at 03:11 on 2026-11-17 local time to the first overlap at 03:50 (capacity 2 was committed at 04:00 in 7358773d), under other work than later, and no log line carries the slot count; so the wait with one slot against two cannot be counted from the log.

'At most three child sessions' comes from the rule in CLAUDE.md: research-tree/ATTACK-AND-COST-RECORD.md line 118 gives it as 'harness fact 1' and research-tree/tcb/cost-inputs.json tags it measured, while the tree's own design calls a fixed three a static level; no measurement is cited for it.

Per-process memory has been sampled on this PC three ways though nothing samples it now: an earlier recorder version wrote the three largest processes with a number each (03:11 to 07:34 on 2026-11-17, unit not stated), the model runner samples its own children's working set, and the suite probe sampled one run's process tree (its sampler code was not kept).

A session blocked on a tool call or a helper makes no model call, so waiting costs tokens only at each wake (a poll or a notice), each wake re-reading the whole context; once the prompt cache lapses a wake pays cache writes, weighted 1.25 to one input token in the tree's cost inputs, instead of cache reads at 0.05.
note: The weights are the tree's cost inputs; that a blocked session makes no model call is reasoning from how a turn works, not a measurement.
